### Pilate’s Cynicism
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/pilates-cynicism
Passage: John 18:37-38
Points:
- Jesus clarifies to Pilate that His kingdom is not of this world and that He came to testify to the truth.
- Submitting to Christ's royal reign requires receiving Him as the ultimate truth and the only way to the Father.
- Listening to and following Jesus requires spiritual regeneration, giving sinners new hearts to believe.
- Pilate exemplifies cynical pragmatism by asking "What is truth?" rather than caring about objective facts.
- Believers must reject modern relativism and faithfully stand for God's objective truth in all matters.

### God Is Truth
Author: David Strain
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/god-is-truth
Passage: John 18:38
Points:
- Pilate's famous question voices cynical resignation to the unknowability of truth rather than an honest pursuit of it.
- Fallen human nature tends to dismiss absolute truth in order to evade moral accountability before God.
- Denying moral absolutes is self-defeating because all moral judgments presuppose an objective standard.
- The great tragedy of Pilate was failing to recognize that Truth incarnate stood directly before him.
- Believers are renewed by the Spirit to know the triune God as the eternal standard and source of truth.
